notes:
CORRECTION (2026-07-17): the ConnectNigeria article originally flagged here as 'worth checking' should NOT be used. Directly fetching articles.connectnigeria.com while researching a later category (Shoemaking) returned a page full of injected gambling/casino spam content, not the site's real articles — a strong sign the domain has been compromised or expired and repurposed. The specific article that looked good in search snippets may still be real, but the domain itself is not safe to add as a live, fetchable source right now. No entry was added here based on it, and none should be added elsewhere either.

CSV integration (2026-07-21): event_decoration_planning_resources.csv, 30 rows. Connect Nigeria appeared again in this CSV (as a Blog this time) — excluded per this file's own existing correction above; this is exactly the category where that domain was first flagged, so good confirmation the caution was warranted.

CHANNELS were the hard part this round: of the CSV's 10 channel picks, only 2 (Preston Bailey, Colin Cowie — both global celebrity event designers) plus 1 Nigerian pick (Eventigo) checked out as real, active, business-relevant YouTube channels. The rest didn't hold up under verification: 'Live Event Solutions' is an equipment rental company with only a 42-subscriber self-promo channel (though their own blog post recommending OTHER channels was a useful lead); 'Shecluded' is a real women's-business fintech platform, not an event-planning-specific channel; '3003 Events' and 'Toyin Obe' returned no findable channel; 'Wedding Planning Institute' resolved to multiple different same-named organizations with no single clear channel; 'Indigo Crystal' and 'PlanPadi' are both real companies with real blogs (kept there) but their YouTube channels were empty or generic, not real content. Channels are at 4/10 (1 existing + 3 new) — genuinely low this round, not for lack of trying. Worth a dedicated follow-up search pass using a different angle (e.g. FeedSpot's event-planning-YouTuber directory surfaced 'Event University' and 'Social Tables' as possible global candidates, not yet verified).
